newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India up in thin trade, some demand seen.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India up in thin trade, some demand seen.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts rallied in thin trade on the back of a firmer trend in Bombay and there was selective demand for some good quality issues.
"The move up on the local market steadied up the GDRs," said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index added 1.75 points, 2.65 percent, to 68.02 points, with the premium over the local market at 13.70 percent compared with yesterday's 12.33.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index rose 44.35 points, or 1.31 percent, 3,427.09, off a day high of 3,464.58.

Traders said there was demand for State Bank of India, up 41 cents at $18.00/$19.00, BSES, up $1.00 at $20.25/$21.25, Ranbaxy, up 69 cents at $18.75/$19.75 and Steel Authority, up 39 cents at $8.25/9.00.

"Bombay is in a 3,250-3,700 trading range and at 3,400, the downside is limited. Investors are a little bit wary of the strong rally on the GDRs earlier this year, but now have another opportunity to get in," said the trader.
On the local market, Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought just $55 million in local stock in the first half of January, compared with an monthly average of $200 million through 1996.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended down 1.40 points, 2.03 percent, at 67.29, a premium of 49.96 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index shed 11.60 points to 678.94.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index gained 3.24 points, 3.26 percent, to 102.67, a premium of 9.40 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index added 39.73 points or 0.55 percent at 7,290.77.
